correctness.rationale: The norm identity is equivalent to sixteen exact complex Gaussian moments. Every at-most-five-node set supports a vanishing real quadratic; four moment pairings force its constant, linear, and radial components to zero, hence its support lies on two perpendicular lines. Positivity and Vandermonde invertibility for three odd moments force an antipodal pair on each line. The diagonal moments then demand a sixth radial moment of six, but such a configuration gives four, contradiction. The displayed strictly positive six-node construction exactly satisfies all sixteen moments. For centrally symmetric six-site configurations, even moments determine two orthogonal axes, all three squared radii and pair masses; odd moments force within-pair equal weights.
